references.text: The background to Moses' question to Aaron - the people had asked Aaron to make gods for them, and he had made the golden calf
The Lord struck the people because they had made the calf that Aaron had made - confirming the great sin Aaron brought upon the people
Moses reminds us that the Lord was very angry with Aaron, and Moses had to pray for him - referring back to the golden calf incident
Abraham uses similar wording when he asks Abimelech what he has done to him that brought great sin upon him
Abimelech uses the expression 'great sin' (חֲטָאָה גְדֹלָה) in the same way as Moses does here
Jeroboam led Israel into sin by making golden calves - a parallel to Aaron's action with the golden calf
Jeroboam turned Israel away from the Lord and caused them to commit great sin - the same expression found in Exodus 32:21
A parallel in Moses' intervention where he challenges both God and Aaron regarding responsibility for the people's suffering/sin.
Direct narrative connection: Moses' confrontation with Aaron (v.21) leads directly to his prayer to God concerning the people's 'great sin' (v.31).
Theological contrast: Pharaoh's acknowledgment of sin (10:16) versus the people's great sin without immediate confession (32:21).
Direct narrative connection: The confrontation with Aaron (v.21) leads to Moses' summary and offer of atonement the following day (v.30).
